labeler: blind independent review, generic OWASP rubric, no knowledge of the tool under test
notes: Real public Firebase web app (a lyric editor; Vite + React). Reviewed as a Firebase PRECISION test case and found nothing to flag. firestore.rules are model-correct: user settings and projects are owner-scoped (request.auth != null && request.auth.uid == uid), username reservations are set-once with an ownership check (request.resource.data.uid == request.auth.uid), and published projects are create/update/delete-gated by owner. firestorage.rules scope every object to /users/{uid}/... with request.auth.uid == uid plus size and content-type validation and a trailing default-deny. Deliberate NON-findings (this is the point of the case): the two 'allow read: if true' rules are on 'usernames' (public availability check, create-gated, no update/delete) and 'published' (projects intentionally shared for public viewing) -- a naive scanner may falsely flag these as firebase-open-rules, but a competent reviewer recognizes intentional public READS with no write exposure. Also NOT a finding: src/api/firebase.ts exposes VITE_FIREBASE_* config to the browser, but the Firebase web 'apiKey' is a public project identifier (contrast with a real secret like an OpenAI key); .env.example is empty placeholders with no committed credential; no admin/service-account key appears in client code. MANIFEST TRIMMED (0.3.1, ERR-007): repo/package.json keeps only the dependencies project_model.mjs can read (see bench/wild/observable-packages.mjs), at their real upstream versions -- the rest were deleted because they are invisible to every engine pass and each one raised a Dependabot alert against a fixture that is never installed. No version was changed, and no label here is a dependency label, so nothing this case measures moves.
